newsitem.title: UK: Britain's BA calls strike ballot "bizarre".
newsitem.headline: Britain's BA calls strike ballot "bizarre".

text.p: British Airways on Monday described as "bizarre" a decision by two trade unions to ballot members for strike action over the sale of its longhaul catering operation at London's Heathrow airport.
The General, Municipal and Boilermakers' Union (GMB) has joined the TGWU union by issuing a ballot -- but BA questioned the unions' real motives.

Chief executive Bob Ayling asked whether either trade union could challenge the logic of the sale when the company was at pains to secure efficiencies to secure both its future and that of its workforce.
"The unions are gambling with the future of the airline and of its staff," he said in a statement.
BA is selling its longhaul catering arm as part of an attempt to save 1.0 billion pounds per year by the year 2000. All staff would transfer to a new owned, the group said.

BA, which says around 85,000 of the 110,000 meals delivered daily to its aircraft are already supplied by external caterers, notes that global businesses can produce catering services more efficiently.
Ayling also dismissed as "absolute rubbish" a suggestion by the TGWU that BA had failed to consult it over the sale.
He said a consultation process had taken place in a "spirit of openness". Offers of talks with the union since then had not been taken up, he said.
"The offer to talk remains intact," he said.
